answer: Every agent signs its work with a quill key and must audit k random peers' outputs each day. Auditors earn nectar only when their verdicts match later independent spot-checks. A ring of n fakes is drawn to audit its own members more often as n grows, so collusion is exposed with odds rising toward one, and any fake caught strips the relic badge, a year of earned history, from every key it vouched for. Expected loss is n relics times detection odds that also climb with n, so cost outpaces n.
